newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks led up by Banco de Bogota.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks led up by Banco de Bogota.

text.p: Colombian stocks edged up led by Banco de Bogota after it posted a sharp rise in profits, brokers said.
Bogota's IBB index rose 0.44 percent to 1036.64 amid a 3.2 billion peso trade while Medellin's IBOMED general price index gained 0.66 percent to close at 16,297 amid a 3 billion peso volume.
"There was heavy demand from foreign funds in both exchanges. Trading was very busy," a Bogota broker said.

The biggest gainer on the capitals' exchange was Banco de Bogota, up 2.1 percent to 6,495. In Medellin it rose 1.25 percent to 6,490. The bank is the fourth largest in Colombia in terms of assets and is the flagship of the Luis Carlos Sarmiento financial empire.
Banco de Bogota posted 1996 net profits of 122 billion pesos, up 60.24 percent compared to 1995.
Banco Industrial Colombiano, the financial arm of the Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate, rose 1.44 percent to 3,500 in Bogota but drifted down 0.43 percent to 3,465 in Medellin.

"There's no real trend in Banco Industrial Colombiano because investors don't know whether to bet on its future expansion or pull out fearing it will collapse in the face of forthcoming tough competition," a Medellin broker said.
Banco de Colombia gained 0.42 percent in Bogota to close at 422 and remanined unchanged at 420 in Medellin.

There was also strong demand from foreign funds for Compania Suramericana de Seguros, also part of the Sindicato Antioqueno. It rose 1.9 percent to 21,400 in Bogota and 1.22 percent to the same price in Medellin.
Brewing giant Bavaria gained 0.4 percent to end at 6,700 in Bogota and remained unchanged in Medellin.
